ShortDescription.Value: DEV TEST BUILD of Traffic: Clear the Way. Unstable - do not use on a city you care about.

Publish.LongDescription:
⚠️ **This is the development build of _Traffic: Clear the Way_. It is not the mod you want.**
Install the normal release instead - this page exists so testers can try changes before they ship.
- Expect rough edges: unfinished behaviour, debug logging, values that change between uploads. - Do **not** run it on a city you care about. Keep a backup save. - Never run it alongside the release version - both register the same systems.
Feedback on a dev build is most useful with `Logs/ClearTheWay.log` attached (switch on "Verbose logging" in the options first).
Release version: https://mods.paradoxplaza.com/mods/151583/Windows
Publish.ChangeLog:
0.1.13.0 - towing that does not eat its own trucks, and a crossing guard.
**The headline: recovery trucks are no longer deleted for sitting in traffic.**
A loaded tow truck that stood still long enough was treated as wedged and removed. In a busy city it reached that threshold just by queueing. Session of 2026-08-09: five trucks deleted in twenty minutes, and each time the wreck was re-armed, a fresh truck was sent, hooked up, stood in the same jam and was deleted in turn. The mechanism never resolved a single blockage; it fed trucks into one.
Standing on a road no longer costs a truck. Only one genuinely OFF the road network - a truck that drove itself into a car park interior - still ends its tow that way. The strikes are still counted and logged: they remain a useful signal that something is wrong there.
**Towing** - Recovery vehicles that wedge on the way TO a wreck are covered now too. Nothing watched them before: the wedge check only ever ran over trucks that were already hauling. A truck that got stuck before reaching its wreck stood there forever - and held the wreck with it, because a claimed wreck waits half an hour for a truck that is never coming. - The dispatcher and the tow depot no longer take the same wreck off each other. Both competed for one maintenance request, so a wreck sitting around 400 m away flipped between them on alternating passes - "the trucks keep having the job taken away too early". The hand-over distance now has 100 m of hysteresis, and each path defends its own assignment for three minutes. - A permanently wedged recovery vehicle no longer escalates in a loop. Its progress record outlived its own give-up deadline, and losing the record restarted the clock - so it escalated for 90 seconds, went quiet for 48, and began again, churning the traffic around it each time. Measured on truck 53038. - A tow truck hauling a wreck home is never slowed by the mod any more. It is not traffic in the way; it is carrying the obstruction off the road. The loop that caused was watched directly: a stuck responder holds everything around it including the loaded truck, so the wreck stays on the carriageway, so the responder stays stuck. - A car in front of a wedged recovery vehicle must be the SAME car for five seconds before it may be flagged or removed. Two cars standing abreast make the game alternate its blocker between them, and the unblock used to fire at whichever one happened to be current - a stranger's car removed for a deadlock it was only half of.
**Pedestrians: a crossing guard** A responder stuck behind a column of cars yielding to someone on a zebra used to end with a car being sacrificed. That is pure waste: every replacement car stops in exactly the same place, and the jam clears itself the moment the pedestrian pulse ebbs. The "civilian cars only" rule could not catch the case either - only the front-most car has the pedestrian as its blocker, so the whole column behind it was fair game.
The case is now recognised, and if the pedestrian itself has stopped making progress the mod acts on the PEDESTRIAN instead: after 30 seconds it is asked to re-route. Nobody is deleted - the citizen takes another path, so its household and job survive. After 90 seconds the guard gives up and the old behaviour resumes.
**Performance** - The sweep that finds cars near an accident ran every single tick: a 600 m search per accident scene plus a main-thread wait. WHO is near a scene is now looked up every eighth tick. WHAT is done to those cars is unchanged and still happens every tick. - The shield that stops responders despawning at a blocked accident swept every police, ambulance and fire vehicle in the city, every tick. It now does so every fourth. - Several diagnostic counters ran on every car near an accident on every tick, producing numbers that are only ever printed with verbose logging switched on. They now run only when it is.
No before/after figure this time, deliberately: the previous build was never profiled, so there is nothing honest to compare against. Measured on this build: the main pass costs about 2.3 ms per simulation tick, the accident sweep 0.5 ms. Frame-rate reports from large cities help most here.
**What to report** Log with "Verbose logging" enabled, plus roughly where it happened. - Frame rate in a big city, particularly if you can compare against 0.1.12.1. - A pedestrian crossing where a responder now waits noticeably longer than it used to. - Any recovery truck that stands still and is never cleaned up. The deletion that used to remove it is gone on purpose, so a genuine wedge is now visible instead of papered over - that is exactly what wants reporting. - Already known, not yet fixed: an ambulance that has picked up its patient gets no arrival help at all on the way back out. One was seen jittering at walking pace beside the scene for around twenty seconds.
